Next, we use the first-order integrated rate law to find the concentration remaining after time $t$:
$$\ln([A]_t) - \ln([A]_0) = -kt$$

$$\ln\left(\frac{[A]_t}{[A]_0}\right) = -kt$$

Now, we solve for the ratio $\frac{[A]_t}{[A]_0}$:
$$\frac{[A]_t}{[A]_0} = e^{-1.386}$$
We know that $e^{-\ln(2)} = e^{\ln(1/2)} = 1/2$. Since $1.386 \approx \ln(2)$, we have:
$$\frac{[A]_t}{[A]_0} = e^{-\ln(2)} = \frac{1}{2}$$

The time elapsed ($t = 60.0 \text{ min}$) is exactly two half-lives, since $60.0 \text{ min} = 2 \times 30 \text{ min}$.
